correctness.rationale: Direct proof: each stable extension chooses exactly one of every privately attacking core/fallback pair, and the chosen cores form any independent set. For an ordered pair of independent sets, its disagreement support is an induced bipartite set and its two color classes are independently flippable on each connected component. The common core set is an arbitrary independent subset outside the disagreement set and its external neighborhood. These are reversible choices, giving every coefficient. Maximum support equals the maximum induced bipartite order, i.e. n minus odd-cycle transversal; deleting colored vertices one at a time proves every intermediate even exponent occurs, and a maximum support has no uncolored external non-neighbors, giving the leading coefficient. Standalone checker enumerated stable extensions directly and independently matched formulas on all 1099 labelled graphs through five vertices and 20 additional six-vertex graphs; finite checks are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Full-text 2026 argumentation-diversity source defines symmetric-difference distance and general computational complexity, not the exact paired-fallback spectrum, no-gap theorem or odd-cycle-transversal leading coefficient. Its shadow-copy gadget adds inter-shadow and cross-copy edges absent from the present corona. Coste-Marquis et al. 2005 supplies the known symmetric-semantics equivalence only. 2026 odd-cycle-transversal work treats graph optimization itself; independent-set/corona literature treats single-set counts. Published mathematical records and general literature were searched for exact, alias, stronger-coverage and polynomial formulations; no statement was found that directly implied the three-part combined formula. Search absence is not proof of novelty and the remaining priority risks are acknowledged.

value.rationale: The private fallback for each core argument is a natural binary-decision representation used in symmetric argumentation. It has exponentially many stable sets even when the core is arbitrary. The theorem determines every disagreement multiplicity and proves a uniform no-gap parity spectrum; its sharp endpoint and count of maximizing ordered pairs identify how precisely the graph odd-cycle-transversal invariant governs logical disagreement. This is a complete structural answer on an unbounded natural family, not a single toy census or a mere computational restatement. The connection makes restricted-graph OCT tools applicable to maximum disagreement without asserting new general-purpose speedups.
